name: Deep-space transit context

original_specification.name: Deep-space transit context
original_specification.description: Deep-space transit context is a conceptual setting for cruise spacecraft; deployed appendages. It combines the specified surroundings with independently managed lighting.
original_specification.representation: Conceptual 3D vacuum setting with explicit astronomical-light ownership
original_specification.geometry: Spacecraft in empty local vacuum with no nearby planetary ground
original_specification.ambient_lighting: One explicit solar source or documented distant source; zero ambient sky
original_specification.scale_policy: Subject scale preserved; distance-dependent solar calibration remains pending; preserve subject dimensions; fit the stage once to an explicit selection, never continuously rescale the CAD model
original_specification.authoring_method: Original procedural geometry and authored relative layout; no downloaded space imagery, real orbit solution or mission-site claim
validation: Vacuum has no atmospheric sky, haze, rain or wind-driven smoke.
Use one environment-owned sun; preserve physically dark unlit regions.
Earth visibility, size and phase require location and ephemeris input; Earth is off by default.
Sunlit-subject exposure does not automatically produce a dense visible star field.

generated_geometry.name: Optional coordinate witness - hide for free flight

geometry_summary.units: millimetres Z-up in OBJ; metres Y-up in glTF/GLB

radiance.source_owner: HDR owns distant room/task patches; the separate Sun owns solar energy

background.limitations: Not a photograph or native renderer output; finite scene geometry is provided separately.

limitations: Vacuum: zero atmospheric sky. Earth and star fields disabled without explicit external inputs.
Relative context is authored, not a mission/ephemeris model.
One 1 mm coordinate witness is included solely to keep portable mesh files nonempty; hide or delete it in free-flight scenes.
Procedural family realization with named contextual components; no claim that every physical detail of the concept has been modeled or validated.
Native glTF import retains geometry and scalar appearances, not arbitrary material extensions or textures.
